violated_contract: Content that the product renders in its own surfaces — a screen, a card, a list, a share link — must be created independently of whether any push channel can reach the user. Selecting recipients by the presence of a delivery token, and then letting that same selection be the only writer of the content, turns an optional and revocable channel into a precondition for the feature existing: a user who declines notification permission gets a permanently empty surface while the feature's toggle still reads as enabled, and no error is surfaced anywhere.
canonical_prevention: Split generation from delivery: the job selects users by the feature's own preference, always generates and stores the artifact, and calls the notifier only when tokens exist. User-initiated 'test' endpoints for the same feature return the generated artifact and report the skipped push instead of failing the request. Regression tests assert a token-less user is selected, gets the artifact stored, and receives no push.
